jobs.title: Environmental Compliance Coordinator
jobs.description:
Position Summary

This position is responsible for the implementation, administration and improving of environmental policies, procedures and programs and the coordination of environmental training.

Essential Functions

Strictly adhere to and enforce all environmental procedures, CAPP (NDEP), OSHA, EPA, RMP Ormat.
Maintain a working knowledge in underground injection control programs, hazardous materials and wastes, universal and solid waste, water and air quality, underground storage tank programs, emergency contingency plans, spill prevention, control and countermeasure, storm water pollution prevention plans, asbestos management, PCB compliance, project mitigation.
Responsible for managing environmental policies and training in compliance with state and federal laws and regulations.
Maintain regulatory database and compliance tracking systems.
Administer environmental reporting requirements on a local, state, and federal level.
Record employee training and monitor training recertification & effectiveness of training conducted.
Assist with identifying time loss environmental incidents and unsafe practices, recommend appropriate corrective action to the Technical Manager.
Maintain contact with emergency response services to ensure exchanged information is current.
Maintain contact with all state, federal, local regulatory agencies.
Ability to obtain and retain appropriate certifications and licensing.
Conduct onsite environmental inspections and reinforce the company vision, values and goals to the team.
Be available (on call) after normal working hours to attend to environmental issues that require immediate responsive action, including environmental audits by regulators.
Must be able to operate a vehicle in a safe manner, enter and exit vehicle without assistance, remain alert while driving for continuous periods of time and read and understand maps.
Work with Environmental Manager for continuous training and guidance on all regulatory environmental requirements. Identify and resolve foreseen issues beforehand.
Assist in budgeting for environmental fees and ensure that environmental invoices are paid at the plant level.

Other Responsibilities

Provide administrative support to the HAZMAT group.
Perform other related duties and projects as assigned by management.

Education, Experience, And Skills Required

An associate degree environmental science, or equivalent preferred.
3 years of experience in an environmental position, or equivalent.
Working knowledge of the Safety field’s concepts, practices, codes, standards, and procedures.
Must have excellent verbal, visual and written communications skills.
Must be able to use and acquire knowledge of a variety of computer software applications in word processing, spreadsheets, database and presentation. Must be proficient in MS Word, Excel, Power Point and use of the Internet.
Possess OSHA 30 Certificate.
Must be willing to travel to areas of operation to perform environmental inspections, and to support and monitor employee environmental training.
Must be able to operate a vehicle in a safe manner.
Must possess at any time a valid driver’s license with a driving record acceptable to ORMAT’s auto insurance carrier.

Physical Requirements

This job requires sitting approximately 30% and standing up to 70%.
The ability to lift 35 lbs.
Must be able to wear any required protective equipment, as required by safety procedures and regulations.
This job requires standing for long periods of time with moderate bending, stooping, and kneeling.
Must be able to climb ladders, platforms, and elevated walkways.
Up to 25% travel.

jobs.title: Environmental Health Officer
jobs.description:
Job No: CoW12378
Location: Whyalla
(Permanent Full-Time)

Are you an Environmental Health Officer seeking a varied, rewarding role with real community impact?
Are you motivated by diverse regulatory work across public health, food safety and environmental protection?
A rostered day off per month and a great working environment on offer!

About the role:

As an Environmental Health Officer, you will play a key role in protecting and promoting public and environmental health across Whyalla.
You will be accountable for ensuring the proper standards of public and environmental health are maintained throughout our community. This is undertaken by monitoring, investigation, and promoting public and environmental health issues with legislative action where necessary.
Reporting to the Regulatory Services Coordinator, you will deliver a diverse range of regulatory, compliance and education-based functions to ensure legislative requirements are met and community health standards are maintained.

Duties will include:

Conducting inspections of food premises, public swimming pools, and personal services to ensure compliance with legislation. 
Investigating public nuisance reports, food safety complaints, and notifiable diseases in collaboration with SA Health.
Delivering education and awareness programs to the community on public and environmental health issues.
Contributing to environmental health planning, policy development, and interagency initiatives across the region.

About you:

We are looking for an individual who has the following:

Relevant qualifications for appointment as a local Authorised Officer under the Public Health Act
Eligibility for membership to Environmental Health Australia
C Class Drivers Licence
National Police Check (or ability to obtain prior to commencement)
Non-prohibited South Australian Working with Children Check (or ability to obtain prior to commencement)
Sharps and infections Waste Handling Training

Students who are nearing completion of a tertiary qualification in Environmental Health or an equivalent discipline are strongly encouraged to apply.

About the Whyalla City Council:

As a multifunctional regional Council, we manage Childcare services, a Library, an Airport, a Cemetery, a Crematorium, Infrastructure and recreational facilities including a Visitor Information Centre. 
We are a progressive Council, committed to the pursuit of excellence and are always looking for opportunities to improve the quality of life for our community, now and into the future.

We stand by and embrace our core values in delivering each of our services: We Deliver, We Belong, We Collaborate, We Serve.

About the benefits: 

Competitive salary + 12% Superannuation with the ability to salary sacrifice.
Company laptop + mobile phone supplied.
Opportunities for career growth and professional development.
Employee Assistance Program and wellbeing support.
Commuting to work when living in Whyalla is no more than 15 minutes.
Rostered day off once a month.
Relocation assistance may be available for the successful applicant, subject to individual circumstances and Council approval.

Further Information and to apply, please visit:
Employment Opportunities | Whyalla City Council

The salary applicable for this role is in accordance with the South Australian Municipal Salaried Officers' Award and Council’s current Enterprise Agreement, paid at Level 5 commencing at $103,143.

Apply:

Applications must include a cover letter expanding on your suitability for this role, addressing the position criteria outlined in the Position Description in no more than three pages.
Applications must include your current resume and must be submitted via Council’s recruitment portal. Scroll down (past the image below) to commence the application process. Please note, the application process will need to be completed in one session.
Applications close 9.00pm, Saturday 7 November 2026. Late applications will not be accepted.
